# Introduction

Item analysis is a common first step in scale development (Lee & Kim, 2019; Park, 2021a). In this synthetic draft we delve into a simple workflow — one that a reader can reproduce with simulated data.

Novak et al. (2018) reported reliability estimates for simulated scales, and later work extended the approach to small samples (Ortiz, 2020). Our aim is to illustrate each step with invented numbers.

# Method

Data were simulated for 30 respondents and 12 items. The items were scored on a five-point scale, and the simulation design is summarized below. Table @tbl:items lists the items.

![Design of the simulation](design.png){#fig:design}

: Items of the simulated scale {#tbl:items}

# Results

Scores differed between the two simulated groups, t(28) = 2.20, p = .03. The difference may reflect the random seed rather than a substantive effect. The DOI 10.5555/synthetic-example-001 is a placeholder from a test prefix.

# Discussion

The workflow is short. Its results are invented and should not be cited.
